recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Verbal judo as giving way to an attack", "body": "Chance described verbal judo as the art of letting an insult fly past like a thrown spear instead of taking it in the face. He explained the strip phrase idea from George Thompson's book, where a speaker says something like \"I appreciate that\" before the \"but\" that carries the real request. Chance said Thompson set this against verbal karate, where words become blows that escalate conflict and burn bridges. He said a key principle was to give way first and then redirect the energy of the attack."}, {"title": "Empathy, paraphrasing, and staying in contact", "body": "Chance described empathy as awareness of how another person feels without taking on those feelings, and he said repeating a person's exact words back to them calmed the exchange and surfaced their real grievance. He called this a technique that is also simply intuitive. Beth said coaches use the same reflection, and she shared a parenting anecdote about calming a tantrum by echoing the child's feeling. Chance added that staying in contact is a core judo principle, and that the line between authentic care and manipulation is intent."}, {"title": "Gabe's research into Dr. George Thompson", "body": "Gabe said he returned to the verbal judo book after a martial arts and padded assailant training career, then watched old seminar footage of Dr. George Thompson. He said Thompson used the phrase black magic about a person's name, and he described a teddy bear parable. Gabe offered his own belief that Thompson's likeness was echoed in a cartoon villain, and he shared number and cipher readings tied to Kent State. Chance said the old videos disappeared from the internet shortly after Gabe raised them, and he remarked that he could not explain why."}, {"title": "Questions, compliance, and the con artist", "body": "Chance described how fact finding questions can feel poor to an agitated person, while open and opinion seeking questions help defuse tension. He said the same opinion questions could generate compliance, and he pointed to polling and voting as examples. Chance retold a hostage story from Thompson's book, noting it may or may not be true. He then summarized the con artist's method as raising expectations and using them to cheat people, and he added that praise before criticism can work but may make later praise seem hollow."}, {"title": "Inner masters, creativity, and the truth movement", "body": "Chance described the master and slave dynamic as something people can enact on themselves, for example in a job they feel forced to keep. He said left brain control over the right brain created that inner enslavement, and that a daily creative practice had helped him loosen it. Gabe added a remark about routine and kung fu. When Beth asked about the truth movement, Chance said he no longer identified his channel with it, and he criticized prison planet narratives as a ready-made ground that people step onto."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Slick Dissident and I return to the subject of Verbal Judo on Beth Martens' King Hero Podcast. It's full of great additional insights into this fascinating martial art of mastering communications.
